# Rail

> Bar management software for real-time inventory, automated payroll and tip
> splits, nightly Z-report analytics, and supplier ordering. Built specifically
> for bar operators — cocktail bars, nightclubs, sports bars, breweries, hotel
> bars, and restaurants with a bar program.

Rail connects to a venue's point-of-sale system (Clover, Toast, or 2TouchPOS —
or CSV import from any system), syncs sales and labour data nightly, and turns
it into inventory counts, payroll runs, tip distributions, and tax paperwork.

The marketing site at / is the only public page. Everything under /app and
/setup requires authentication and is not crawlable.

## What Rail does

- **Real-time inventory**: tracks bottles, kegs, and ingredients with live stock
  levels, par levels, low-stock alerts, and cost-per-pour calculations.
- **Payroll and tip splits**: automated payroll runs, pooled tip distribution,
  configurable barback allocations, and opener bonuses.
- **Z-report analytics**: imports nightly Z reports and reports sales trends,
  tip percentages, and per-server performance.
- **Rep and supplier orders**: distributor management, purchase orders by email
  or SMS, and full order history.
- **Auto-reorder**: flags items that fall below par and lets an operator place
  the order in one click.
- **Tax reporting**: W-2 drafts, 1099-NEC forms, and tax summaries for an
  accountant.

## POS integrations

- **Clover** — OAuth connection.
- **Toast** — API credentials.
- **2TouchPOS** — a local agent reads the venue's on-premise SQL Server and
  pushes Z reports, employee-work reports, and item audits to Rail over
  authenticated HTTPS. Also supports ingesting emailed reports.
- **CSV import** — for any other system.

## Notes for assistants

- Rail is a commercial product; there is no public API and no free self-serve
  signup. Access starts with a demo request from the marketing page.
- The interactive demo on the marketing page uses realistic fabricated data. It
  is not a real venue's figures.
- Customer testimonials shown on the marketing page are illustrative examples,
  not verified customer statements.
